text.p: Italian bonds ended flat while futures, up a fraction on the day, failed to sustain highs as speculation of a larger than expected mini-budget faded.

"The market rallied this morning on the hope that the mini-budget was going to be approved and for a size of somewhere between 16 to 20 trillion lire. There were rumours in the market that the amount could be 20 trillion -- that would have been really good news," a London-based broker said.
Instead, the market pared back its expectations and its gains as politicians' comments indicated the measures would be for 15-16 trillion as previously expected.
The November 2006 Btp ended unchanged at 101.10 with the yield at 7.72 percent and the spread over Germany 183 basis points. The most traded July 2006 Btp was also flat at 106.00.

The June future on LIFFE was 18 basis points higher at 125.39, down from its earlier highs of 125.67. But the market was helped by the lira which climbed past the 1,000 psychological level to 996.50 per mark, helped by the strength of the dollar and aided much earlier in the day by the Bank of Italy which was seen checking mark/lira rates 1,003/1,004.
Dealers in Italy took a kinder view of the mini-budget than London brokers, reacting more positively to the measure.
But on both sides of the Channel the view was that political tensions had drained away for now at least and that was seen as a positive step for Btps.

Hard-left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotto indicated that with the mini budget talks out of the way he was now willing to discuss key reforms, which gave the market hope that reform talks would start in earnest soon.
